item.title: Delta tech outage, Mother Nature fuel latest air travel disruption as Thanksgiving looms
item.description:
【AI 精简版】 AI-trimmed version. An LLM deleted boilerplate sentences from the original article and left the rest verbatim. The original link at the end is the only authoritative source. (Clean-up failed for this item, so the body is a truncated excerpt of the original.)

Why it is here: original reporting, concrete detail

Editorial note: This story has been updated with new information.

The Thanksgiving travel rush is off to a messy start.

The culprit: bad weather and the latest tech outage to hit a major U.S. company.

Delta Air Lines delayed or canceled thousands of flights on Sunday after a problem with a key system that automates weight and balance calculations.

The disruption led to mass delays at its Atlanta mega-hub — the world’s busiest airport — and cascaded to other airports around the country.

This content is hosted by X.

View this post on X

By 6:15 p.m. EST Sunday, more than half of all flights had been delayed at Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport (ATL), according to FlightAware. That included hundreds of departing flights — and planes headed to the airport.

Late Sunday afternoon, Delta said it had restored its automated system. But the disruptions continued to climb as the carrier worked to get operations fully back on track.

More coverage from TPG:

- Post-FAA meltdown: Is air travel ready for Thanksgiving?

- Air travel meltdowns: 9 ways the TPG team navigates flight woes

- Flight canceled or delayed? Here's what to do

How many Delta flights are affected?

Delta's residual flight disruptions climbed through the day on Sunday.

- As of early Sunday evening, roughly 6 in 10 Delta mainline flights had been delayed, per FlightAware — a total of more than 1,900 departures.

- Regional subsidiary Endeavor Air, which operates Delta Connection flights, reported another 260 delays, per FlightAware.

- Roughly 100 additional Delta flights were canceled Sunday, about 2% of its planned schedule for the day.

Around 70% of the flight disruptions were due to the tech issues, the airline said. The rest were tied to Sunday's weather problems, and air traffic control delays that resulted.

“We thank our customers for their patience and our people for their professionalism," Delta said in a statement to TPG.

Bad weather fuels flight delays, diversions

Travelers had other problems to contend with Sunday, too.

Mother Nature also snarled air traffic at some major hubs.

Low cloud ceilings and poor visibility fueled flight delays and led to dozens of planes getting diverted.

New York’s LaGuardia Airport (LGA) was most heavily affected, with nearly 60% of all departing and arriving flights delayed Sunday, per FlightAware.

This content is hosted by X.

View this post on X

42 flights headed to LGA on Sunday were diverted to other airports, according to aviation analytics firm Cirium.

Many of those flights landed instead in Philadelphia; Albany, N.Y.; Harrisburg, PA; and Syracuse, N.Y.

Another air travel disruption

These disruptions come a week after one of the most chaotic weekends at airports in recent memory.

More than 18,000 flights were canceled last weekend after an outage on Nov. 13 to critical Federal Aviation Administration technology.

Last week, a brief technical outage at United Airlines also fueled a host of flight delays.

What to do if you’re affected: This week, the TPG team put our heads together to offer some of our top tips for navigating a travel meltdown. Here’s what to know.

Can you get a refund if your flight is delayed or canceled?

If your flight is canceled or significantly delayed, you’re entitled to a refund under U.S. Department of Transportation policy — but only if you choose not to fly.

Know why your flight was delayed or canceled

If you get stranded in Sunday’s travel mess, it pays to know what the reason was for the disruption.

If you get stuck because of Delta’s tech outage, the carrier may be willing to pay for any hotel, meal and ground transportation costs you incur — if it’s a major delay. See details at FlightRights.gov.

The carrier on Sunday acknowledged it was providing those accommodations to passengers "when necessary."

If you get stuck because of bad weather, it's less likely your airline will offer any sort of compensation. But keep your receipts: If you paid for your trip with a credit card that has travel insurance, you might be able to file a claim and seek reimbursement.

Looking ahead to Thanksgiving

Sunday’s travel woes also coincide, of course, with the start of the Thanksgiving travel rush — with airports expected to be very busy with holiday travelers over the next few days.

All eyes are on next Sunday — Nov. 29 — which could be the busiest day of the year to fly.

Last year, the Sunday after Thanksgiving set the record as the most crowded day ever at U.S. airports.

item.title: How to avoid petty theft while traveling

Quick summary

- Petty theft is a risk in many popular travel destinations, especially crowded tourist spots and public transportation hubs.

- Travelers can reduce their vulnerability by minimizing valuables, blending in with locals and staying alert in busy areas.

- Using theft-resistant bags, securing belongings and splitting up valuables are effective strategies to deter thieves.

- Travel insurance may offer theft protection, but coverage varies, so reviewing your policy details is important.

What to consider

- Thieves often work in teams, creating distractions to target distracted travelers.

- Public transportation and tourist attractions are common hotspots for pickpocketing incidents.

- Scams can take many forms, from unsolicited help to aggressive sales tactics, so maintaining awareness is crucial.

Why it is here: useful vocabulary, clear explanation

Quick summary

- Dining reservation platforms like OpenTable, DoorDash, Seated and Resy now offer rewards for booking and completing restaurant reservations, each with distinct earning and redemption models.

- OpenTable awards points redeemable for dining credits or experiences, DoorDash provides credits for future orders, Seated offers a percentage back as rewards for gift cards and Resy grants additional loyalty points at participating venues.

- The value and structure of rewards vary: OpenTable is widely available but offers lower returns, DoorDash is best for smaller bills, Seated can be most lucrative for larger spends, and Resy delivers a strong return but is currently limited in scope.

- All programs are free to join, but eligibility, reward expiration and redemption options differ, so choosing the best platform depends on your dining habits and location.

What to consider

- Some programs require app activations or enrollment steps, and certain benefits are only available in select cities or on specific devices.

- Rewards may expire after periods of inactivity or have usage restrictions, such as not covering taxes and fees or being limited to certain brands for gift card redemption.

- Stacking reservation rewards with eligible payment methods can further enhance overall value, but terms and availability vary by platform.

- Key perks include free checked bags, expedited security screening, lounge access, ride-hailing and food-delivery credits, and hotel privileges like early check-in or complimentary breakfast.

- Many travel cards offer statement credits for airport security programs and ride services, as well as elite status with hotels or rental car companies to streamline your journey.

- Selecting the right card depends on your travel habits and which benefits will save you the most money or time during peak travel periods.

What to consider

- Some benefits, such as free checked bags or lounge access, may require enrollment or payment with a specific card and can have restrictions on eligible companions or locations.

- Application and enrollment for airport security programs should be completed well in advance, as processing times can be lengthy.

- Hotel and rental car elite status benefits often require linking loyalty accounts and confirming eligibility before travel.
